__comment: The Blacksmith's own workbench (doc 297): a squat bowl furnace of three stone courses daubed with soil, a clay crucible sunk in its top and a fire mouth at the front, beside a flat casting stone with two bar moulds cut in it. Tier 1 Hearthblock model from tools/hearthblock/art/tier1.mjs.
Blacksmiths make it at the crude workbench from a log, four Rough Stones and a Soil. Like the mason's bench it keeps no wood identity.

Copper bars are made here as a batch (batch_hours in the recipe): charged in 12 s, it melts by itself on the world clock, then a Blacksmith takes the cast bar off the stone (COLLECT). The charge part (batch_model) shows while a batch is on. Copper fittings are hammered cold here, with no wait.

batch_heat: its heat_source counts only while a batch melts (WorkshopBatch.update_heat), never when it stands idle or once the copper has set (doc 44, the Smelter's heat rule). The heat is a first figure, to tune in play.
The casting stone's top stands 0.375 blocks high; the furnace's rim 1.125, inside the collision regions.
description: A bowl furnace of daubed stones with a clay crucible, beside a casting stone with bar moulds: the Blacksmith's own workbench. Copper ore and coal melt in it for a few hours, then a Blacksmith takes the cast bar off the stone. Warms its room while it melts. Occupies a 2 by 1 space.
